title: Policy DSL for staged rollouts and safety nets
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
We need a concise, testable Policy DSL and enforcement path for staged rollouts that supports canaries, percent ramps, feature-flag driven cohorts, and automated rollback gates. The DSL will be the canonical source of truth for Redwood Console rollout pages, router behavior in the serving runtime, and the simulator used by SRE and release engineers.

Problem:
Current rollout configurations are represented as ad-hoc JSON blobs in multiple repos, leading to divergence between console UI, runtime enforcement, and simulation tests. We lack:
- a predictable, expressive language for ramps (step/linear/feedback-driven), cohorts (hash-based stable canaries), and multi-layer gates (SLO, infra-health, perf-anomaly),
- standardized auto-rollback definitions tied to real metrics,
- a single enforcement path with deterministic semantics across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.

Proposal:
1) Define a compact Policy DSL (YAML-first syntax) with these primitives:
   - phases: named steps with duration or traffic target, e.g., "phase: canary 1% for 30m",
   - ramps: step | linear | feedback, with parameters (step-size, step-interval, max-duration),
   - cohorts: selection by stable hash (customer_id, tenant, region) or by label (internal, beta),
   - gates: checks that can be SLO-based (error-rate, p95 latency), anomaly detectors (changepoint on error-rate), infra-health (GPU mem pressure, queue depth), or external signals (manual hold),
   - actions: continue, pause, rollback, notify, migrate-traffic-to(model-variant),
   - tolerances and thresholds: error_rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m => action=rollback; p95 latency increase > 50% vs baseline => pause and notify,
   - kill-switch scope: deployment-level and system-wide.

2) Enforcement model: DSL -> validation & simulation -> signed rollout artifact -> routed by environment-specific controller (hosted/dedicated/private). The controller interfaces with the serving runtime to change traffic weights and watch metrics surfaced by Console tracing and Prometheus.

3) Observability & safety nets:
   - Integrate rollout artifacts with Console so each rollout renders phases, current metrics, and predicted next-step.
   - Automated rollback triggers implemented as streaming rules in the metric agent with debounce (windowed evaluation) and dry-run alerts.
   - Provide a simulated execution harness that can run historical traffic, inject faults, and validate DSL semantics before creation.

Acceptance criteria:
- DSL spec doc and grammar published in Confluence and committed to repository: repo rollouts/policy-dsl/spec.md.
- Parser + validator implemented (unit tests covering 95% of grammar).
- Simulator able to run at least two canonical scenarios: (a) canary 1% -> linear to 100% with SLO gate, (b) cohort-based rollout to internal users only.
- Runtime controller POC that can accept a signed rollout artifact and execute a 3-phase canary in staging.
- Console shows rollout visualization for the POC and exposes abort/force-continue controls.
- Runbook added: playbook for manual intervention and post-rollback incident steps.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Expressiveness vs simplicity: rich DSL enables advanced behaviors (multi-metric gates, conditional actions) but increases surface area for bugs and cognitive load. We will start with a minimal core set and iterate.
- Where to evaluate anomaly detectors: in Console (centralized) vs local agents (edge)? Centralized evaluation simplifies semantics, but increases latency to react. We'll prototype centralized rules with an eventual plan for edge-guard observers in dedicated/private deployments.
- Backwards compatibility: need migration strategy for existing JSON blobs. Provide a converter and deprecation timeline.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Sprint 1 (this cycle): spec, grammar, parser, and validator + example artifacts.
- Sprint 2: simulator and unit tests; console visualization prototype.
- Sprint 3: runtime controller POC and staging rollout; e2e test and runbook.

Links & artifacts:
- Confluence spec (draft): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/rollouts/policy-dsl-draft
- Design notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/rollout-dsl-design
- Simulator repo PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-sim/pull/88
- Console mockups: https://figma.com/redwood/console-rollout-views

Risks:
- Incorrect or noisy metric thresholds causing spurious rollbacks. Mitigation: conservative defaults, dry-run mode, 2-step manual enablement for high-impact deployments.
- Drift between controller and runtime in private deployments. Mitigation: signed artifacts, versioned API, audit logs.

Next steps:
- Draft DSL grammar and push to rollouts/spec branch (owner: Luis).
- Build validator and key unit tests (owner: Maya).
- Schedule review with SRE and Console PMs next week.
